independent_computation.method: The scenario tuple (roster composition, levels, builds, fight length) is NOT reconstructible from data/ or docs/math-foundations.md — grep for 'mandate_abyssal', 'ending_health', '438.6' and '661.1' across the whole export returns nothing. So the leaf value cannot be re-derived from scratch. What CAN be derived independently is which sourced amplifier the leaf pair encodes, by inverting the survival identity under the integer-max-health convention.
independent_computation.identity: ending_health = H0 - D, so D_old/D_new = (H0 - 438.6)/(H0 - 661.1) = A, where A is the extra damage-taken multiplier present in the old value and absent in the new one. Inverting: H0 = (A*new - old)/(A - 1).

independent_computation.conclusion_of_inversion: Every surviving hypothesis (A = 1.07 with H0 = 3839/3840, A = 1.12 with H0 = 2515, A = 1.0625 with H0 = 4220/4221) says the same thing: the old leaf carried EXACTLY ONE additional wiki-sourced conditional damage-taken amplifier on participant[2], and the new leaf does not. The 'both amplifiers dropped' readings are rejected — one arithmetically (1.1984 admits no integer max health), one on roster evidence (1.19 demands a max health below the level-18 base-health floor of the champion pool).
independent_computation.rule_test: Both amplifiers in this scenario are strictly conditional per the quoted wiki text: Unmake applies only to ENEMY champions of the wearer, inside 700 units, and only to MAGIC damage; Command's Vulnerable applies only to an enemy champion that was actually IMMOBILIZED, and only for a 4 s window. A 'roster' fight (the corpus supports enemies + allies lists per data/worklists/e8d-task.md: 'a /api/calculate fight WITH AN ALLY in the roster (enemies + allies lists are supported)') necessarily contains participants that fail at least one of those conditions. Applying an amp to such a participant is an over-application; there is no wiki-sourced reading under which a participant should receive MORE than the conditions grant. Therefore the only modeling error consistent with the observed direction (participant[2] taking less damage after the change) is that the old value over-applied one conditional amplifier, and the new value withholds it.
independent_computation.direction_test: An under-application bug cannot be repaired by a change that RAISES ending_health. Since the leaf moved up by exactly one amplifier's worth (6.25%-12% of the damage stream, matching the 7% and 12% figures quoted from the cache and nothing else), the change is a narrowing of a conditional amp to its sourced condition, which is what the cached wiki text mandates.

limitations: The scenario input tuple (roster, levels, builds, fight window) is not present anywhere in data/ or docs/math-foundations.md, so the leaf could not be recomputed end-to-end from first principles; the verification is an inversion of the leaf pair against the sourced amplifier magnitudes plus the integer-max-health convention.

The inversion cannot distinguish WHICH of the two amps was withheld (7% Mandate at H0 in {3839,3840} / {4220,4221}, or 12% Abyssal at H0 = 2515) — only that exactly one was, which is sufficient to rule on direction.

If participant[2] genuinely satisfied both conditions (an enemy inside the 700-unit aura, immobilized within the last 4 s, taking magic damage), the old value would be the correct one. That reading is not supported by the scenario being a 'roster' case, whose purpose is exactly to exercise per-participant scoping of these conditional amps.
verdict_rationale: The leaf pair encodes the removal of exactly one wiki-sourced conditional damage-taken amplifier (Abyssal Mask Unmake +12% magic, or Imperial Mandate Command Vulnerable +7%) from participant[2]. Both amps are conditional in the cached wiki text (enemy-only + 700-unit aura + magic-only; immobilized-only + 4 s window). In a roster fight, a non-lead participant failing one of those conditions must not receive that amp, so the higher ending_health (661.1) is the wiki-consistent value. The 'both amps dropped' over-correction readings that would justify a both_wrong verdict are excluded: 1.1984 admits no integer max health under the corpus-wide integer-health-rounding convention, and 1.19 requires a max health (1832) below the level-18 base-health floor of every cached champion but Yuumi.
